main_body: A bare, dead gothic tree: a vertical trunk with spreading bare branches, a few dark crow shapes, and a flared root base. Organic, with no flat horizontal top surface.
top_band: none; the column at x=24 goes from the dark outline (rows 3-7) straight into brown trunk tones with no light horizontal band. Branches and trunk are vertical or diagonal forms.
evidence: This is a bare tree, an organic form without a flat top. The trunk, branches and base are drawn as a natural silhouette, so there is no top, front-face or opening structure to judge. Under the organic kind, the usual 3/4 rules for flat tops do not apply. The trunk has a flared root base and branches that overlap with a bit of depth. The only failures to look for are a flat front elevation or a top-down plan, and neither is present. It reads as a normal map tree.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 7 colours per tile. The references have 427-567 colours and a median of about 108 per tile. 93% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is near-black and reads as a sticker outline, while the references have tinted outlines (0% neutral). The trunk has roughly 4 brown steps with some bark grain, but the shading is shallow and the branches are mostly flat two-tone strokes. It sits well below the Beodeul references in richness and shading.
